label: Missionary aims
quiz: What did Catholic missionaries seek to do?
Spread their religion
Prove every resident already shared one belief
Erase the need for historical evidence
Require present-day students to profess a faith
retry: What does a missionary's hope for acceptance establish by itself?
An aim, not everyone's actual belief
Universal conversion across all communities
Every household's private motive
The absence of earlier religious traditions
hard: A classroom report says studying missionaries requires a prayer. What correction fits?
Historical learning can examine aims and evidence without religious practice
Religious practice is necessary for every history question
Students must reveal their faith to receive a score
Only one religious identity can study the past

label: Missionary sequence
quiz: Which named example belongs to the later 1565 expedition?
Augustinian friars led by Urdaneta arriving with the expedition
Every missionary order arriving in 1521
Magellan returning after his death
All communities accepting one faith on one day
retry: Why distinguish a recorded 1521 event from continuing missionary work?
They concern different stages and do not establish universal conversion
They prove every participant had identical beliefs
They were one identical event in one place
No later religious activity needs study
hard: A marker dates a missionary arrival. Which additional claim needs separate evidence?
The responses and beliefs of particular communities afterward
That the marker describes an arrival
That a named religious group appears in the record
That the event can be placed in a sequence

label: Languages and materials
quiz: What does the surviving 1593 Doctrina Christiana help establish?
Production of a religious teaching text in Spanish and Tagalog
Every resident's reading and acceptance of its teachings
Identical understanding across every language
The creation of all local language knowledge
retry: Why distinguish producing a book from its reception?
Circulation, reading, understanding and acceptance need further evidence
A printed object guarantees every reader's belief
All communities necessarily read the same book
No object can be historical evidence
hard: A page uses a local language, but no reader account is supplied. Which report is careful?
Describe the communication effort and leave particular readers' responses open
Declare every speaker converted
Invent a reader's speech as original testimony
Assume all people interpreted the text identically

label: Colonial context
quiz: Which question connects missionary activity with its setting?
How did religious aims, political power and local decisions interact?
Why did all participants have one identical motive?
Why did power never matter to any encounter?
Which invented speech proves everyone agreed?
retry: Why should an official's political aim not be assigned to every family?
It is not evidence of each family's private reasons
All people always shared the official's plans
An office title reveals all private beliefs
Missing testimony proves universal consent
hard: A report names a religious institution and claims no pressure could exist. What should be checked?
Evidence of actions, power and local responses in that setting
Only the institution's name repeated
An assumption that institutions guarantee consent
A fictional speech replacing missing sources

label: Responses and viewpoints
quiz: A baptism record describes a ceremony. What does it not establish alone?
Every participant's private understanding or everyone's belief
That a ceremony was recorded
That the record can be investigated
That a named event appears in a source
retry: How should acceptance, adaptation and resistance be used?
As responses to investigate in particular settings and periods
As permanent labels for every member of a religion
As identical actions with no differences
As measures of people's worth
hard: An account describes one setting but claims identical belief everywhere. What revision fits?
Keep the supported setting and identify the unsupported universal claim
Erase the event solely because the broad claim fails
Treat every missing voice as proof of agreement
Require the learner to adopt a faith before judging the evidence
